reason: Butler handoff actions (notes, settings/theme/navigation, downloads, credentials, devices, diagnostics, etc.) return pending_browser_apply and change nothing until the requesting web app applies them, but Core could not tell a terminal turn from a browser turn, so Butler offered them in nebula-chat and the terminal printed 'Tool finished'. ChatCompletionRequest gains optional client_surface ('browser' default for existing web clients, 'terminal' from nebula-chat and the terminal Assistant); it is saved in the provider turn request_snapshot and harness turn metadata, passed to ButlerCapabilities on direct, queued, resumed and retried turns, and adds a terminal note to Butler's instructions. On the terminal surface ButlerCapabilities.invoke refuses any result in the pending_browser_apply state (decided from the action's result, not a name list, so a new handoff is covered and notes create/update stop being refused once they save in Core) with fixed browser_only guidance; the terminal labels an older Core's handoff receipt as needing the Nebula web app. Python: test_butler_client_surface.py (new: real handoffs incl. notes.delete refused on terminal and unchanged on browser, a synthetic future handoff action refused by result for read and change routes, Core-saving change still works, request/surface validation, provider API turn end to end with snapshot and instructions, harness turn metadata/prompt/capabilities; all 7 fail on origin/main), terminal shell and chat CLI tests for the sent field and the handoff notice (5 fail on main), the product-help search test for the new docs (fails on main) plus the index digest/sync tests, and existing Butler capability, settings browser-intent, harness Butler gateway and queued Butler follow-up tests around the changed paths.
exclusions: No UI, native or Playwright changes: the web app omits client_surface and keeps today's behavior, and ui/src/settingsCatalog.ts is unchanged because no setting changed.
